title: Health Quest ATL
subtitle: A 90-day community health campaign for APS families, built around telehealth adoption, audience segmentation, media operations, and live activation.
summary: Bivines Group designed and launched Health Quest ATL for VE360 on behalf of Atlanta Public Schools: a 90-day campaign to increase family adoption of Hazel Health, a free telehealth resource available to APS students. Starting from a sub-3% enrollment rate, the work combined campaign brand creation, a five-segment audience strategy, radio and press coordination, community events, and an independent incentive structure that protected APS from attribution and liability risk.

carousel.title: 1. Overview
carousel.heading: A district-scale health campaign built in 90 days
carousel.content:
Health Quest ATL - Atlanta, Georgia - Spring 2023

We designed and launched a 90-day community health campaign for a 52,000-student school district sitting on a free telehealth resource almost no one was using. Starting from a sub-3% enrollment rate, we built a purpose-built campaign brand, a five-segment audience strategy, a multi-channel media operation, and a live event series - all within a structure that protected the district from attribution and liability risk. The result was 500,000+ targeted impressions, four-station radio placement, and three flagship community events executed on schedule.

carousel.title: 3. The Situation
carousel.heading: A free service with almost no adoption
carousel.content:
Atlanta Public Schools launched a free telehealth service - Hazel Health - in Fall 2022. Every student in the district was eligible. Physical and mental health visits, at school or at home, at no cost to families regardless of insurance. By early 2023, fewer than 3% of eligible families had completed the consent form required to access it. The service worked. The need was real. The problem was that almost no one knew it existed - and among those who did, most hadn't acted.

APS had already attempted internal communications through its central office and school administrators. It hadn't moved the numbers. The district needed something its own channels couldn't provide: an independent campaign that could motivate families without creating liability exposure for the district, and a strategy sophisticated enough to reach people who weren't reachable by a single message.

VE360, an Atlanta-based education communications agency, was engaged to solve the problem. They brought in Bivines Group to design and lead the full campaign - including the strategic architecture, brand creation, media direction, and execution management across vendors and channels.

carousel.title: 4. The Ask
carousel.heading: More than a communications plan
carousel.content:
VE360 needed more than a communications plan. What the work actually required:

- Audience diagnosis - identify why families weren't enrolling, not just that they weren't
- Campaign brand creation - build a standalone initiative with its own identity, separate from APS, to absorb all promotional and incentive activity
- Behavioral activation strategy - design a system that motivated the largest non-participating segment (42% motivation gap) without relying on district resources or creating district liability
- Multi-channel media execution - secure earned and paid placement across Atlanta radio, television, print, and online publications
- Event strategy and execution - design and execute community-facing stakeholder events tied to campaign milestones
- Vendor management - scope, commission, and direct a media subcontractor (PDM Agency) through a full PR execution cycle
- Institutional risk architecture - structure the campaign so APS received all the benefit of incentive-driven engagement without direct attribution to district operations

carousel.title: 5. The Approach
carousel.heading: Segment first, then build the campaign system
carousel.content:
We started with a market analysis, not a messaging brief. Before writing a single headline, we segmented the 38,000-family target audience by the type of barrier keeping them from enrolling. We identified five distinct gap segments - motivation (42%), knowledge (20%), awareness (13%), culture (11%), and privacy (8%) - and built the campaign strategy around closing the two largest: motivation and awareness. A single campaign message would have reached one segment. We needed an architecture that could reach all of them simultaneously through different channels and different appeals.

The central strategic decision was structural, not creative. APS could not legally or practically incentivize families to complete a consent form. So we designed around that constraint by creating Health Quest ATL as a fully independent campaign entity - its own brand, its own operations, its own liability footprint. The district plugged in as a beneficiary. Every enrollment triggered by the Q42 Challenge accrued to APS without APS having to sponsor or manage it. That separation was not an afterthought - it was the load-bearing wall of the entire campaign.

From there, execution ran on two simultaneous tracks: a direct communications plan deployed through APS's internal channels (staff, teachers, family messaging) and an external motivation campaign built around the Q42 Challenge - a 42-day competition with prizes, weekly social media challenges, live events, and sponsor-funded rewards. Both tracks fed the same call to action: complete the Hazel consent form.

carousel.title: 6. The Work
carousel.heading: Brand, segmentation, media, events, and PR
carousel.content:
Campaign Brand Development
We created Health Quest ATL from the ground up - name, identity, positioning, and operational structure. The brand was designed to operate independently of APS, absorb all incentive and promotional activity, and generate enrollment without creating district exposure. The Q42 Challenge was its primary activation mechanism.

Market Analysis and Audience Segmentation
We conducted a structured market analysis that identified five behavioral gap segments within the 38,000-family target audience. Each segment was sized by percentage, defined by the specific barrier driving non-participation, and mapped to a corresponding campaign intervention. This segmentation drove all channel, message, and sequencing decisions.

Media Strategy and Subcontractor Direction
We scoped, commissioned, and directed PDM Agency through a full earned media campaign. Targets included V103, KISS 104.1, Hot 107.9, WAOK 1380, Star 94.1, and 92.9 The Game on radio; 11 Alive, Fox 5 Atlanta, WSB-TV, Atlanta News First, CW69, and Atlanta & Company on television; and nine print and online publications including the Atlanta Journal-Constitution, Rolling Out Magazine, and The Atlanta Voice. Spokesperson placement was secured on four stations in a single morning.

Event Design and Execution
We designed and executed three flagship community events: a Minority Health Town Hall (week of April 17) convening Atlanta health experts for a district-wide community forum; a Mental Health Teen Summit (week of May 8) centering youth voices on mental health; and a Q42 Sponsors and Awards Reception (May 19) to close the campaign. We also managed ongoing neighborhood registration drives, school drop-in activations, and sponsor ambassador engagements throughout April and May.

Communications Planning and PR
We produced and distributed multiple press releases placed on the wire and sent directly to local news agencies, timed to campaign milestones. A week-by-week PR activities calendar governed all media pitching, influencer outreach, PSA distribution, and interview coordination from March 13 through May 15.

carousel.title: 7. The Impact
carousel.heading: 500,000+ impressions and a live community campaign
carousel.content:
The campaign ran on schedule across its full 90-day window. Confirmed outcomes:

- 500,000+ targeted impressions across radio, TV, print, online, and live events
- 4 Atlanta radio stations secured for spokesperson placement - aired on a single morning across V103, WAOK 1380, Star 94.1, and 92.9 The Game
- 3 flagship stakeholder events executed on schedule: Minority Health Town Hall, Mental Health Teen Summit, Q42 Sponsors and Awards Reception
- Multiple press releases distributed via wire and direct to local press, timed to campaign milestones
- PDM Agency scoped, directed, and delivered as media subcontractor under Bivines Group management through the full campaign window
- Health Quest ATL launched as a fully operational independent campaign entity - brand, website, social channels, and event infrastructure built within the pre-launch window

carousel.title: 8. The Deliverables
carousel.heading: A full campaign stack, not just outreach copy
carousel.content:
Comprehensive Outreach Strategy (21-page PDF) - Full campaign plan covering market analysis, audience segmentation, campaign architecture, launch strategy, communications strategy, event strategy, and milestone timeline. Delivered to VE360 March 6, 2023.

Five-Gap Market Analysis - Structured diagnostic segmenting 38,000 eligible APS families by behavioral barrier type (motivation, knowledge, awareness, culture, privacy) with percentage sizing and corresponding intervention mapping for each segment.

Health Quest ATL Campaign Brand - Purpose-built independent campaign identity including name, positioning, and operational structure designed to absorb all incentive and promotional activity on behalf of APS.

Q42 Challenge Architecture - Three-phase contest design (Connect, Engage, Reward) with weekly social media challenges, scoring logic, prize and sponsor framework, and a 42-day campaign timeline.

PR Outreach Plan - Week-by-week execution calendar for media pitching, press release distribution, influencer engagement, radio scheduling, PSA placement, and spokesperson coordination across a 500,000+ impression campaign.

Media Outlet Target List - Curated contact list spanning 5 radio stations, 6 television outlets, and 9 print and online publications with prioritized outreach sequencing.

Press Releases (multiple) - Wire-distributed and locally placed releases covering the APS x Hazel Health partnership, the APS x Health Quest ATL partnership, the Q42 Challenge launch, event announcements (Minority Health Town Hall, Mental Health Teen Summit), and the Rewards and Recognition ceremony.

Interview Recap Document - Post-campaign media placement record documenting secured radio appearances by station, air time, and interview subject - including four-station single-morning placement on V103, WAOK, Star 94.1, and 92.9 The Game.

Event Design and Run-of-Show (3 flagship events) - Concept, purpose statement, panelist coordination, and production framework for the Minority Health Town Hall, Mental Health Teen Summit, and Q42 Sponsors and Awards Reception.
